title: Document skipped releases explicitly to prevent user confusion
context: v1.34.0 was git-tagged but superseded before npm publication; all features rolled into v1.35.0. Without documentation, users viewing 1.34.0 release notes will search npm and find nothing, creating support friction. Touches invariant(s): con_039cee7367 (Memory hygiene is the agent's job, done without waiting for the human: accept shipped roadmap proposals, settle provenance-repair escalations (apply the true commit or drop), re-anchor or stale findings, and land the resulting capture commits through a PR. Only decisions that need genuine product judgment are queued for the human.).
decision: Add explicit note in CHANGELOG.md and site/changelog.html stating v1.34.0 was tagged but not published to npm, with all changes shipping in v1.35.0.
consequences: Users immediately understand why v1.34.0 isn't available on npm
Clear feature lineage from skipped to actual release
Reduces support inquiries about missing/orphaned versions
Release history remains transparent and auditable
alternatives_rejected: Delete v1.34.0 entry — loses historical context and tag rationale
Publish both 1.34.0 and 1.35.0 to npm — introduces duplicate feature versions
Silently omit documentation — causes user confusion and broken expectations
